land.cliopatria: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia

predecessors.note: Same state: the Kingdom page dates the kingdom from 10 May 1881 ('Kingdom proclaimed'); this dossier starts at Greater Romania (December 1918), where Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Romania' row begins and the united-principalities dossier ends.

land.text: '28 November. The union of Bukovina with Romania is declared.' '1 December. The union of Transylvania with Romania is declared.'

predecessors.note: Transylvania, Banat (part), Crisana, Maramures and Bukovina; Hungary renounced its claims at Trianon (1920). Bessarabia came from no dossiered state (Sfatul Tarii, the National Council of Bessarabia: 'proclaim the union of Bessarabia with Romania' earlier in 1918). The land came to Romania through the united-principalities-of-moldavia-and-wallachia dossier (Bukovina 28 November 1918 and Transylvania 1 December 1918 are its ledger 27 and 28; austria-hungary ledger 35 hands both lands to that dossier in October 1918), so this dossier does not book those gains again; it holds the land from its found event of December 1918 and records the Trianon recognition of June 1920.

302,753 km2 against the page's 295,049 km2 for 1940 ('including territories later ceded') is a ratio of 1.03. [Fix pass: the Romanian contest and occupation of Hungary in 1919-1920 are drawn from the ledger on the east bank of the Tisza and across Hungary except the Lake Balaton area.]

300,845 km2, 1,908 km2 less than 1919, within the shape's precision. Trianon (1920) had Hungary renounce 'all the claims of the Austro-Hungarian Monarchy over Transylvania'; some Western powers recognised Bessarabia by the 1920 Treaty of Paris, which never took effect because Japan did not ratify; 'a few border settlements were exchanged' with the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes in 1923 (no area given).
300,959 km2: unchanged within the shape's precision; no territorial event on the page between 1923 and 1940.
301,005 km2. 10 February 1938: Carol II instituted 'a short-lived royal dictatorship' (a regime change, no border change).
301,073 km2, ratio 1.02 to the infobox 295,049 km2 (1940, before the cessions).

245,867 km2 is the state after the Soviet occupation of 28 June-3 July 1940 (301,073 - 50,762 = 250,311) and before the 30 August Vienna Award (-43,104) and the 7 September Craiova cession (-7,142). It is a mid-1940 snapshot: the ledger carries the two later losses with their months, and the 1941 shape starts from the year-end state.

region.text: 'Romania gained all of Transylvania' (the page); the region is the researcher's broad Transylvania with Crisana, Maramures and the Romanian Banat

ledger.note: 4 June 1920: the Treaty of Trianon, signed 'on 4 June 1920' and in force 26 July 1921, gives Romania 'all of Transylvania, which was home to 2,800,000 Romanians'; 'The central parts of Banat were later assigned to Romania' (Crisana and Maramures are not named on the page, so the region is the researcher's reading). This is the legal recognition of land Romania already held from the unions of 1918 and the 1919 shape (booked in the predecessor dossier and in this dossier's found event); it mirrors the hungarian-republic loss of June 1920 and adds no land to the 1919 shape. The Banat page: 'When the province was divided in 1920, Romania was assigned an area of 18,966 km2' (9,276 km2 to the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, 284 km2 to Hungary). The Kingdom of Romania page, earlier source of this event: Hungary 'renounced in favor of Romania all the claims of the Austro-Hungarian Monarchy over Transylvania' and 'a few border settlements were exchanged' with the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes in 1923 (no area on either page). [Replaces the earlier Banat-only gain of 1920 and the 1918 gains of Bessarabia, Bukovina and Transylvania, after review eu-21-b.]

ledger.note: March 1944: the Romanian administration of Transnistria ends. The Transnistria Governorate page: 'A Romanian civilian administration governed the territory from 19 August 1941 to 29 January 1944'; the Red Army 'entered Transnistria on 14 March 1944'; 'On 15 March 1944, Potopeanu ordered the withdrawal of all remaining personnel from the region'; the infobox gives 'Disestablished: 1 April 1944' ('The Germans officially took over the region on 1 April 1944'). March 1944 follows the withdrawal order; the page's three dates differ, hence confidence 2. wars.outcome: Romania retook Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina in July 1941 and administered Transnistria from 19 August 1941; the Soviet Second Jassy-Kishinev Offensive of August 1944 and the coup of 23 August ended it, with the armistice of 12 September 1944.

certainty.note: The union of Bessarabia, Bukovina and Transylvania was declared in 1918 and the Banat and Hungarian frontiers were still moving until Trianon; the Romanian army was in Hungary in 1919.
Trianon, Saint-Germain and the Treaty of Paris (Bessarabia, recognised by some powers only) fixed the frontiers.

Ultimatums, the Vienna Award and Craiova gave sharp lines in 1940 (Vienna Award and Craiova are dated treaties), but the Soviet frontier of 1940-41 and 1944 and the Transnistria Governorate are approximate.
Frontiers of 1 January 1941 with Northern Transylvania restored, confirmed in the 1947 Paris treaties.

notes:
Cliopatria rows: 'Kingdom of Romania' (1919-1947, Q203493) is Greater Romania. Cliopatria's 'Romania' row (1990-2024, same Wikidata id) is the post-communist republic and the 1948-1989 communist state has its own row ('Socialist Republic of Romania'): different states, not merged. The Old Kingdom (1881-1918) is the united-principalities-of-moldavia-and-wallachia dossier; this dossier starts in December 1918 to avoid overlap. Counterpart note: Romania's gains of Transylvania and Banat are dated to the declarations of 1918 and to Trianon (1920); the Hungarian dossier dates its losses to Trianon (4 June 1920, from the Trianon page) and notes the 1918 unions. Pages silent: the 1923 border exchange with Yugoslavia (no area), Neuilly (Southern Dobruja went back to Romania in 1919 per the Bulgarian dossier, not on a page opened here), the date of the 'Legionary Romania' name, the date and extent of the Transnistria Governorate (the Romanian administration spanned the Dniester-Bug land and Odessa; extent not on the page). The 1940 shape is a mid-year snapshot (after the Soviet occupation, before Vienna/Craiova). Region names the gazetteer may lack: none beyond 'Transylvania (broad)', which exists. Counterpart 'Sfatul Țării (National Council of Bessarabia)' has no dossier (the Moldavian Democratic Republic of 1917-1918 would be the dossier name; not on a page opened). Transnistria Governorate (1941-1944) and Bessarabia 1941-1944 as provinces are modelled here as an occupation of Soviet land (Transnistria) and a gain (Bessarabia, N. Bukovina), following the page's wording 'occupied'.

Fix pass after review eu-21-b (2026-11-01). Applied: (1) the gains of Bessarabia (1918), Bukovina (28 November 1918) and Transylvania (1 December 1918) are deleted: the predecessor dossier books all three (ledger 22, 27, 28) and the found event's region, the 1919 shape, holds them; the Banat-only gain of 1920 is recast as the Trianon recognition (4 June 1920, 'Transylvania (broad)', counterpart hungarian-republic; the Trianon page: 'Romania gained all of Transylvania'). The counterpart 'Sfatul Tarii (National Council of Bessarabia)' is therefore no longer used. (2) The Romanian contest and occupation of 1919-1920 (ledger and war zone) now lie in Hungary east of the Tisza and across the post-Trianon territory minus a Lake Balaton disc; the earlier spec fell in Slovakia and Ruthenia. (3) The Transnistria occupation ends in March 1944 (Transnistria Governorate page: 15 March withdrawal order; 29 January 1944 end of civilian rule and 1 April 1944 infobox date differ; confidence 2). (4) The Soviet administration of Northern Transylvania until 9 March 1945 (Second Vienna Award page) is an occupation pair with the Soviet Union (the reviewer's optional fix, applied). Not settled: the 1923 exchange of border settlements with the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes (the Banat page, opened in the fix pass, does not mention it; the Kingdom page names it without an area). Soviet side: union-of-soviet-socialist-republics has no mirror of the Transnistria occupation, the 1944 Soviet administration of Northern Transylvania or the Romanian occupation of 1941-1944 (routed in the report). I do not disagree with the reviewer on any finding.
